sources.title: The Limited Virtue of Complexity in a Noisy World
sources.version_notes: Crossref identifies posted-content and OpenAlex identifies a preprint. The inspected file advertises an SSRN latest-version link; no version of record was established.
sources.abstract: Portfolio performance depends on the noise level in features, and more complex models do not necessarily lead to better performance when features are not perfectly observed.

evidence.quote: While complexity has the potential to enhance portfolio returns, its benefits depend on access to high-quality data and robust infrastructure.
evidence.note: AI-assisted extraction draft. Confirm against the source before assigning a verdict.

evidence.quote: In fact, beyond a certain point, adding more features reduces out-of-sample prediction performance and portfolio Sharpe ratio.
evidence.note: Negative-control excerpt. The AI draft may recommend contradiction, but only a human may confirm it.

evidence.quote: As Figure 5 shows, the out-of-sample R2 and Sharpe ratio both increase as the feature dimension increases from low to moderate, but eventually decline once the model becomes more complex.
evidence.locator: PDF page 42, Section 5.3 and Figure 5 on page 43
evidence.note: The paper states that results are averaged across all stocks and five repetitions; retain that scope during review.
